claims.text: The initial MgAlCuZnGd alloy is as-cast and non-equilibrium.
The initial alloy is a supersaturated single-phase B2/BCC material.
The MgAlCuZnGd alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
Isothermal annealing at moderate temperature nucleates and grows Al-rich intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries.
Increasing the annealing duration increases the grain-boundary precipitate volume fraction.
Formation of Al-rich precipitates depletes Al from the surrounding matrix and reduces matrix Al activity.
The precipitation-induced compositional redistribution alters local galvanic potentials.
Precipitation promotes formation of a more adherent, Al-enriched oxide scale.
Disruption of micro-galvanic coupling lowers the aqueous corrosion current.
Formation of the proposed adherent Al-enriched oxide scale slows high-temperature oxide growth.
Annealing will reduce corrosion current density by at least 30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealing will decrease mass gain during 100 h oxidation at 800 °C by at least 25% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed mechanism remains valid for annealing temperatures from 300 to 500 °C and durations up to 100 h.
The proposed mechanism applies to alloys of similar composition with density below 6 g/cm3.
The controlled comparison is between an as-cast sample and a sample annealed at 400 °C for 50 h, with identical corrosion and oxidation protocols.
A failure to increase precipitate fraction by at least 20% is specified as a falsifying result.
Corrosion current density and oxidation mass gain both remaining within ±10% of baseline is specified as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says precipitation depletes Al from the matrix and lowers matrix Al activity, while also asserting that this promotes an Al-enriched oxide scale. These statements are not necessarily impossible together, but the required Al-transport or selective-oxidation step is omitted, leaving an unresolved mechanistic tension.
